newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbeks plan to form aircraft leasing company.
newsitem.headline: Uzbeks plan to form aircraft leasing company.

text.p: Uzbekistan plans to set up an aircraft leasing company, which it hopes will boost sales of planes produced at its aircraft factory in the capital Tashkent, Vadim Kucherov, Director General of the factory, said on Monday.

The factory produces Ilyushin-76 four-engine turbo-jet transport planes with a cargo capacity of 50 tonnes. It has recently started assembling new Ilyushin-114 turbo-prop 64-seat two-engine passenger planes.

"Offers of Ilyushin-76 and Ilyushin-114 on condition of financial leasing and with 30-45 percent of their price paid in advance must substantially increase sales of the planes produced at our enterprise," Kucherov told Reuters.

In Soviet times the factory produced up to 60 Ilyushin-76 planes annually, the main buyer being the Soviet army. But after the collapse of the Soviet Union and the severance of economic ties with Moscow, output plunged to just five planes last year.
Several new Ilyushin-114 planes are now undergoing test flights, and Kucherov said he hoped that by the end of next year his enterprise would assemble around 60 of them.

He said the new leasing company -- Uzavialeasing -- would be set up by the Tashkent aircraft factory, Russia's Ilyushin Aviation Complex, Uzbekistan's Bank for Foreign Economic Activity, and probably the State Property Committee.
Kucherov said the charter capital of the leasing company would be $50-$100 million, and all documents needed to legally form the company must be signed by the end of this summer.
